{"text": "The promotion was decided before the meeting.

I have spent thirty years in the rooms where careers are decided, and here is what I can tell you: nobody in that room ranks your work. Someone describes you in one sentence, everyone nods, and the decision moves on. You find out on Tuesday.

That sentence is your career. And most people have never heard theirs.

The inside work is deciding what you want said about you, then making it true in the conversations you keep postponing. The ask. The boundary. The honest feedback.

On Thursday, October 29 at 7 PM ET I am hosting a free, live masterclass called The Corporate Advantage. One hour on how you are being read by decision makers, how to close the gap without losing yourself, and how to become indispensable on purpose. Link in bio.

{"text": "The most expensive sentences in a career are the ones said without a plan.

I have watched talented people lose years of hard-earned trust in one meeting, because they walked in with a feeling and no decision about what they were there to say. The room did not remember the point. It remembered the moment.

So before the hard conversation, write down the one thing you need them to walk away with. Say that. Let the rest go.

{"text": "Here is a leadership habit I learned early and have never regretted.

Before you correct someone, go look. Not at what a peer told you. Not at what you assume. At the work itself. You inspect what you expect, and then you have the conversation from facts.

It takes ten more minutes. It saves you a good employee, and it saves you from being the leader who manages by rumor.

Leaders: what is one thing you expect from your team that you have not personally inspected this month?", "media": ["https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rodbrinson/tbs-social-graphics/main/brands/dawn-kirk/2026-10/q-inspect-01.jpg"], "providers": [{"network": "instagram"}], "publicationDate": {"dateTime": "2026-10-17T06:45:00", "timezone": "America/New_York"}, "autoPublish": true, "draft": false, "shortener": false, "firstCommentText": "#leadership #management #inspectwhatyouexpect #hrexecutive #dawnskirk", "instagramData": {"type": "POST", "isAiGenerated": false}}

{"text": "Every productivity system I have ever used, I learned in a minivan.

Pick them up, get them changed, get myself changed, get everybody where they need to be, and still walk in on time. Nothing in corporate America has asked more of my calendar than that.

So when someone tells me they cannot find the time, I ask a different question: what are you treating as optional that a mother would not?

Moms in leadership, I see you. What is the one skill parenting gave you that your job gets the benefit of?", "media": ["https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rodbrinson/tbs-social-graphics/main/brands/dawn-kirk/2026-10/q-motherhood-01.jpg"], "providers": [{"network": "instagram"}], "publicationDate": {"dateTime": "2026-10-18T06:45:00", "timezone": "America/New_York"}, "autoPublish": true, "draft": false, "shortener": false, "firstCommentText": "#workingmom #worklifeintegration #womeninleadership #executivecoach #dawnskirk", "instagramData": {"type": "POST", "isAiGenerated": false}}
